cxf_lu_factorize in src/basis/lu_factorize.c consumes 47-65% of total solver runtime, growing with problem size. This is the #1 performance bottleneck.

|---------|------------|-------------------|

## Root Cause
Current implementation uses dense Gaussian elimination without fill-in reduction. Specifically missing:
1. Markowitz pivot ordering — minimize (r_i-1)*(c_j-1) fill-in metric

4. Threshold partial pivoting — |a_ij| >= u * max|a_kj| with u=7.8e-3

## V2 Spec
- product_form_inverse.md: Full sparse LU algorithm
- tolerances_constants.md Section 3: Markowitz tolerance 1/128
- numerical_stability.md Section A: 4 refactorization triggers

## Acceptance Criteria
- LU factorization uses Markowitz ordering
- Sparse triangular solves skip zeros
- cxf_lu_factorize drops below 25% of runtime on beaconfd
- All 16 currently-passing Netlib problems still pass","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"tobias.osborne@itp.uni-hannover.de","created_at":"2026-02-17T22:25:34Z","created_by":"tobiasosborne","updated_at":"2026-02-17T22:28:11Z"}

## Root Cause
get_row_coeffs extracts row coefficients from CSC format by scanning all column pointers — O(nnz) per row. Called once per constraint during presolve. CSR format (mat->row_ptr) exists but is not used here.

- simplex_phases.md (cxf_simplex_preprocess): Compute activity bounds once at initialization
- pivot_operations.md (cxf_pivot_update): Update bounds incrementally during pivots
- No per-iteration or per-phase row scanning prescribed

## Fix
1. Use CSR format (mat->row_ptr/col_idx/row_values) for O(nnz_row) row access
2. Cache activity bounds after first computation
3. Avoid re-scanning during Phase I setup

## Acceptance Criteria
